title: Proper-surjective local constructibility of nearby-cycle cohomology
statement: Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and let $f:X\to S$ be of finite presentation [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $\Lambda$ be a finite commutative ring with $m\Lambda=0$ for an integer $m\geq1$ invertible on $S$. Let $K\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ be a bounded constructible complex [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. For every integer $q\geq0$ there is a proper surjective morphism $p:T\to S$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism] such that, writing $X_T=X\times_ST$, $p_X:X_T\to X$, and $f_T:X_T\to T$, the sheaf $\mathcal H^q(R\Psi_{f_T}(p_X^*K))$ on $V_{f_T}$ [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles] is constructible [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf]. This assertion concerns nearby cycles of the base-changed family; no comparison with the inverse image of $R\Psi_fK$ is asserted, and no $\Psi$-goodness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.27(2), printed p. 37, last sentence applying Orgogozo Theorem 8.1 to a bounded constructible input; finite coefficient specialization. Orgogozo author draft at https://www.cmls.polytechnique.fr/perso/orgogozo/articles/Modifications%20et%20cycles%20proches%20sur%20une%20base%20g%C3%A9n%C3%A9rale.pdf states the modification version as Theorem 7.1, printed pp. 16–17, with its constructibility proof in Section 9; numbering differs from the 38-page published version.

proof.text: There are finitely many irreducible components of $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components]. Give them reduced structures $S_i$. Each $S_i\to S$ is a closed immersion and hence finite, thus proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], and their finite disjoint union is surjective. It suffices to construct the claimed cover separately over each integral $S_i$: composing the covers with $S_i\to S$ and taking their disjoint union gives a proper surjection. Both the new family and its vanishing topos decompose over these open-and-closed components, so the finite-stratification definition [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf] gives the result componentwise. No comparison with the nearby cycles over $S$ is needed. We therefore work over an integral base until the last step.

source.place: Section 9.2: reduction to an integral base.

proof.text: For an integral affine base use [lem-trf-nearby-spread-out] to write $(X\to S,K)$ as the pullback of $(X_0\to S_0,K_0)$, with $S_0$ integral affine of finite type over $\mathbf Z[1/m]$ and $K_0$ bounded constructible. We will first prove the assertion over such arithmetic bases and their finite-type modifications/alterations, which are excellent Noetherian of finite dimension. Steps 3--16 do this. Steps 17--18 return to $S$ and then glue finitely many affine opens. The spread-out assertion alone is not being used to transfer constructibility: the transfer at the end uses full $\Psi$-goodness and its actual comparison.

source.place: Sections 2.1, 9.2; Lu--Zheng Theorem 4.27(2), p. 37.

proof.text: On the arithmetic schemes fix the lexicographic induction $(\delta,r,d)$: $\delta$ bounds the dimension of the integral base, $r\geq-1$ is the truncation degree, and $d$ bounds the geometric fibre dimension of a proper map. The assertion is that every bounded constructible input in $D^{\geq0}$ acquires constructible $\tau_{\leq r}R\Psi$ after a modification; we may require the new pair to be $\Psi$-good by [lem-trf-orgogozo-good-modification]. Module sheaves on these small sites are Grothendieck [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Right derived direct image is left t-exact [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing], so $r=-1$ is immediate. Every time a constructibility assertion has been obtained, first arrange goodness by that theorem if necessary; exact pullback and the comparison then preserve it under any further base change. Thus finitely many successful modifications can be combined by [lem-trf-modifications-zariski-refinement]. We prove the proper case for every $d$ at fixed $(\delta,r)$ before passing to arbitrary finite-type maps at that same pair of parameters.

source.place: Section 9.2, the assertions constr(delta,r,d) and their induction order.

proof.text: An alteration suffices at any induction stage. Start with a good pair on an integral base, using [lem-trf-orgogozo-good-modification]. If $T\to S$ is an alteration on which the relevant cohomology is constructible, apply [lem-trf-alteration-finite-refinement] to get modifications $\widetilde T\to T$ and $S'\to S$ and a finite surjection $\widetilde T\to S'$. Goodness of the original pair identifies the nearby cycles on these bases with pullbacks; hence the good sheaf on $S'$ pulls back to a constructible sheaf on $\widetilde T$. Apply [lem-trf-psi-constructibility-descent] to each degree. This produces a modification of $S$ with the desired truncation. The same reasoning applies when finitely many extra modifications on $T$ were needed. Pullback preserves constructibility here directly: pull back the finite source and base strata, and pull back their finite locally constant module sheaves [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf].

source.place: Sections 1.5, 9.1.5 and 9.2: constructibility is h-local after goodness.

proof.text: The finite-type assertion follows once the proper assertion at $(\delta,r)$ is known for all $d$. Work on an affine open of the base and a finite affine open cover of the source. An affine finite-type source embeds in affine space and has a dense projective compactification by [lemma-nagata-quasi-affine-immersion-affine-space-exists] and [det-nagata-affine-opens-projective]. Extend its bounded constructible complex by $j_!$; this is exact [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact] and constructible, since its strata are the old strata and the complementary closed subset, where its stalks are zero [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks]. Apply the proper assertion for some fibre bound [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound]. Smooth source exchange for the open immersion [lem-trf-oriented-nearby-smooth-source-pullback] restricts the resulting nearby cycles to the original family. The open source subtopoi cover the vanishing topos [lem-trf-oriented-source-localization]. A finite refinement of their strata yields constructibility globally; common modifications exist by [lem-trf-modifications-zariski-refinement]. There is no requirement that compactification preserve $d$: all $d$ have already been proved.

source.place: Sections 3.3 and 9.2: compactification and the passage from proper to finite type.

proof.text: For a proper map, reduce bounded nonnegative complexes to sheaves. Successive truncation triangles [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] express $K$ through its finitely many constructible $H^aK[-a]$, $a\geq0$. For $a>0$, degrees through $r$ of $R\Psi(H^aK[-a])$ use only degrees through $r-a$ of $R\Psi H^aK$, already covered by the lower-$r$ induction. Only the sheaf $H^0K$ requires the current degree. The long exact cohomology sequences and closure under subquotients and extensions on the vanishing topos [lem-trf-oriented-constructible-subquotients] finish this reduction. Triangulatedness and left t-exactness of $R\Psi$ are supplied by [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated] and [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing]; all earlier truncations can be kept on common refinements as in Steps 3--4.

source.place: Section 9.2 and the finite-constant dévissage of Section 3.4.

proof.text: For a constructible sheaf $E$, [lem-weil-pbc-constructible-module-finite-pushforward-embedding] supplies $0\to E\to E'\to Q\to0$ with $E'=\bigoplus p_{i,*}\underline{M_i}$, $p_i$ finite and $M_i$ finite modules. Ordinary proper-image finiteness [lem-weil-pbc-etale-proper-direct-image-finiteness] (fibre bound zero) makes $E'$ constructible, so $Q$ is constructible by [thm-constructible-serre]. Lower-$r$ induction handles $Q$. In [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles], $\bar p_i\psi_{fp_i}=\psi_f p_i$; derived composition [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] therefore gives $R\Psi_f Rp_{i,*}=R\bar p_{i,*}R\Psi_{fp_i}$. Finite ordinary direct image is exact [lemma-weil-pbc-finite-direct-image-exact] (forget scalars to test exactness), and finite oriented direct image is exact [lem-trf-oriented-proper-image-constructibility]. Thus the constant-module case makes $H^{\leq r}R\Psi E'$ constructible. The exact sequence $H^{j-1}R\Psi Q\to H^jR\Psi E\to H^jR\Psi E'$ and [lem-trf-oriented-constructible-subquotients] finish for $j\leq r$. Finite $p_i$ preserve the fibre bound. The constants are arbitrary finite modules, not necessarily free.

source.place: Section 3.4 as used in Section 9.2; Lu--Zheng Theorem 4.27 proof: replace Lambda by finite constant modules.

proof.text: We now prove the proper constant-module case. Cover the source by the finite disjoint union of its reduced irreducible components, and take its Cech proper hypercover. Its levels are proper over the original source. In [lem-trf-oriented-nearby-hypercover-spectral-sequence], the terms of simplicial degree $i>0$ contributing to total degrees at most $r$ require nearby-cycle degrees only through $r-i<r$; lower-$r$ induction therefore treats them. Applying [lem-trf-oriented-proper-image-constructibility] to their bounded truncations gives constructible cohomology after the proper oriented direct images. There are only finitely many relevant simplicial degrees and the abutment filtration is finite, so [lem-trf-oriented-constructible-subquotients] finishes once degree zero is treated. Its sources are integral. This reduction also handles nonreduced sources, without silently replacing a scheme by its reduction.

source.place: Section 9.2, integral-source reduction and proper cohomological descent.

proof.text: If the integral proper source does not dominate $S$, it factors through its reduced closed image $F$, with $\dim F<\delta$. Lower-base-dimension induction on $F$ gives a modification $F'\to F$ with the required constructibility and goodness. Apply [lem-trf-modification-closed-image-lifting] to $F'\to S$: after a modification $S'\to S$ there is a finite surjection $G\to F\times_SS'$ and a map $G\to F'$. Goodness pulls the desired sheaves from $F'$ to $G$. By [lem-trf-nearby-finite-base-descent] the family over $F\times_SS'$ is good, and [lem-trf-psi-constructibility-descent] descends its cohomology constructibility from $G$. Finally [lem-trf-oriented-closed-base-extension] identifies nearby cycles of the proper family over $S'$ with exact closed extension from $F\times_SS'$, which preserves constructibility. Thus this case uses strictly smaller $\delta$, regardless of its fibre dimension.

source.place: Section 9.2 and Section 3.2: nondominant case and lifting the closed-image modification.

proof.text: For a dominant integral proper source use [lem-trf-plurinodal-proper-hypercover]. After an integral alteration $T\to S$, its degree-zero source is a finite disjoint union of semistable towers and a proper source with nowhere dense image. The latter is covered by Steps 8--9. Positive simplicial degrees of the hypercover are covered by lower-$r$ induction just as in Step 8, using [lem-trf-oriented-nearby-hypercover-spectral-sequence] and [lem-trf-oriented-proper-image-constructibility]. Only finitely many levels matter in degrees through $r$; combine their modifications. It remains to handle the towers in degree zero. Their lengths equal the generic fibre dimension of the original proper dominant source, hence are at most $d$. The alteration is converted back to a modification by Step 4 after the tower calculation. All the alterations here have base dimension $\delta$; the recursion in the positive levels is in $r$, not an unjustified decrease of source dimension.

source.place: Section 9.2, displayed proper-hypercover spectral sequence and its degree-zero reduction.

proof.text: A tower of length zero is $1_S$. Its nearby cycles of $\underline M$ are $p_2^*\underline M$ by [lem-trf-nearby-smooth-source-exchange], so are constructible and concentrated in degree zero. For a tower of length $e>0$, write $X\xrightarrow{h}Y\xrightarrow{g}S$, where $h$ is its last semistable curve and $g$ has fibre dimension $e-1<d$ (or, if $e<d$, use the already proved lower-$d$ case directly). The datum [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data] includes a closed $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ finite over $Y$ containing the nonsmooth locus; write $j:U=X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$. Set $C=R\Psi_{gh}\underline M$ and $F=H^rC$. Lower-$r$ induction already makes $\tau_{\leq r-1}C$ constructible. We will show constructibility of $F$ in Steps 12--15.

source.place: Section 9.3, semistable tower and the finite singular-locus datum.

proof.text: The arithmetic schemes $X$ and $Y$ are Noetherian of finite dimension. For the proper curve $h$, [lem-weil-pbc-etale-proper-direct-image-finiteness] makes $Rh_*\underline M$ a bounded nonnegative complex of constructible sheaves (its degrees are $0,1,2$). Lower-$d$ induction for $g$ therefore applies both to $\underline M$ and to $Rh_*\underline M$, making their nearby cycles constructible through degree $r$. Arrange their goodness and keep them on a common modification using [lem-trf-orgogozo-good-modification] and [lem-trf-modifications-zariski-refinement]. The tower pulls back to a tower. These uses of ordinary proper-image finiteness are on the finite-dimensional arithmetic schemes only; it is not being applied over the original arbitrary Noetherian base.

source.place: Section 9.3, the lower-dimensional tower and its proper curve direct image.

proof.text: On $U$, the last curve is smooth. Smooth source composition [lem-trf-oriented-nearby-smooth-source-pullback] gives $\bar j^* C\simeq\overline{h|_U}^{\,*}R\Psi_g\underline M$. Thus $\bar j^*F$ is constructible by Step 12: exact inverse image pulls back the finite strata and their finite locally constant module sheaves [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf]. By open/closed source localization [lem-trf-oriented-source-localization], $A=\bar j_!\bar j^*F$ is a constructible sheaf on $V_{gh}$. This establishes constructibility on the smooth part without a trait-finiteness theorem.

source.place: Section 9.3, smooth-locus calculation.

proof.text: We next show $\bar h_*F$ constructible. Apply $R\bar h_*$ to $\tau_{\leq r-1}C\to\tau_{\leq r}C\to F[-r]$ [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle], using [lem-pc-right-derived-functor-triangulated]. The truncation isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-truncation-iso] identifies $H^r(R\bar h_*\tau_{\leq r}C)$ with $H^r(R\bar h_*C)$. The long exact sequence contains $H^r(R\bar h_*C)\to\bar h_*F\to H^{r+1}(R\bar h_*\tau_{\leq r-1}C)$. Since $\bar h\psi_{gh}=\psi_g h$ [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles], the derived composition isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] gives $R\bar h_*C\simeq R\Psi_g Rh_*\underline M$. Its degree-$r$ sheaf is constructible by Step 12. The last sheaf is constructible by Step 11 and [lem-trf-oriented-proper-image-constructibility]. Their images and the resulting extension are constructible by [lem-trf-oriented-constructible-subquotients], proving the claim. This is the truncation argument of Lemma 9.3.1, with the actual derived-functor truncation theorem cited.

source.place: Section 9.3 and Lemma 9.3.1, printed pp. 22-23.

proof.text: By [lem-trf-oriented-source-localization], $0\to A\to F\to\bar i_*\bar i^*F\to0$ is exact. Set $\pi=h i:Z\to Y$, which is finite by the tower datum. Applying $R\bar h_*$ gives $\bar h_*A\to\bar h_*F\to\bar\pi_*\bar i^*F\to R^1\bar h_*A$. Here finite closed direct image is exact [lem-trf-oriented-proper-image-constructibility], and derived composition [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] identifies the third term with that finite pushforward. The outside terms are constructible by that lemma and constructibility of $A$; the second term is constructible by Step 14. Hence the third is constructible by subquotients and extensions [lem-trf-oriented-constructible-subquotients]. Finite direct image detects constructibility [lem-trf-oriented-proper-image-constructibility], so $\bar i^*F$ is constructible. Exact closed extension and the displayed localization sequence then show $F$ constructible. This finishes the last curve, with no invocation of the theorem being proved.

source.place: Section 9.3, finite singular-support argument after Lemma 9.3.1.

proof.text: Steps 11--15 prove the tower case needed by Step 10. The finite filtration of [lem-trf-oriented-nearby-hypercover-spectral-sequence] and [lem-trf-oriented-constructible-subquotients] then proves the dominant proper constant-module case. Steps 8--9 prove the other constant-module cases; Steps 6--7 give all bounded nonnegative constructible inputs. Every recursive call has smaller $\delta$, or smaller $r$, or the same $(\delta,r)$ with smaller fibre bound $d$. Step 5 extends the conclusion to finite-type maps only after all proper fibre bounds have been treated. This closes the induction. All combinations involve finitely many sheaves, hypercover levels and modifications; the unbounded simplicial object is not being treated by an infinite sequence of alterations.

source.place: Sections 9.2-9.3: closing the three inductions.

proof.text: For general bounded $K_0$ on the arithmetic model, shift it into $D^{\geq0}$. A finite bound $d$ for the fibres exists by [lem-fin-finite-type-fibre-dimension-bound]. If its cohomological interval after shifting is $[0,b]$, [lem-trf-nearby-dimension-bound] puts its nearby cycles in $[0,b+2d]$, uniformly after base change. Apply the proved induction with $r=b+2d$, then undo the shift. We obtain a modification of $S_0$ on which all nearby-cycle cohomology is constructible; ensure full goodness as well using [lem-trf-orgogozo-good-modification] and a common refinement [lem-trf-modifications-zariski-refinement]. These further pullbacks preserve the result by goodness. This bound is used to choose one finite truncation, not as a constructibility theorem.

source.place: Sections 2.1 and 9.2; Lu--Zheng Theorem 4.27(2), p. 37.

proof.text: Pull that model modification back to the original integral affine $S$ and take the reduced closure of its isomorphism open. By [lem-trf-nearby-spread-out] this is a modification $S'\to S$ with a map to the modified model. Full goodness [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles] identifies $R\Psi_{f_{S'}}K_{S'}$ with the inverse image of the model's nearby cycles. This inverse image is exact, so also identifies each cohomology sheaf. It preserves constructibility: pull back the two finite stratifications in [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf]; their oriented-product restrictions carry inverse images of finite locally constant module sheaves. Thus the conclusion holds over integral affine bases of arbitrary Noetherian dimension. Cover an arbitrary integral Noetherian $S$ by finitely many affine opens and apply [lem-trf-modifications-zariski-refinement] to their modifications. Goodness keeps their constructibility on the refinement, and the finite open covers and finite strata refine to one finite stratification. This proves the integral-base case.

source.place: Section 2.1 and the local-to-global reductions preceding Section 9.

proof.text: Finally apply the integral-base construction to the finitely many reduced components from Step 1 and take the disjoint union $T$ of the resulting modifications. Its map $p:T\to S$ is proper and surjective. On each component the cohomology of $R\Psi_{f_T}(p_X^*K)$ is constructible; the componentwise finite strata combine to finite strata on $X_T$ and $T$, giving constructibility on $V_{f_T}$ by [def-trf-oriented-constructible-sheaf]. In particular its degree-$q$ cohomology is constructible for the prescribed $q\geq0$. The proof has established this for the newly pulled-back family, exactly as stated, using good intermediate pairs only inside the construction.

source.place: Section 9.2; Lu--Zheng Theorem 4.27(2), p. 37.

proof_origin.place: Section 9, especially 9.2-9.3 and Lemma 9.3.1; finite-module adaptation in Lu--Zheng v7 Theorem 4.27, pp. 36-37. Sources read online, not installed in literature/.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q45-2f46f549b (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read all 19 steps of the item, all six new statement-only nodes and the statement of every cited node; I made no changes. No step invokes the theorem itself, and every recursive call lowers a parameter of the induction (base dimension, truncation degree r, fibre bound d): 7 calls Q at r-1, 8 and 10 call positive hypercover levels at r-i, 9 calls closed images at a smaller base dimension, 12 calls the shorter tower at d-1, and Step 5 (finite type) is used only after all d. Step-by-step checks: Step 4 makes the pair good first, then descends through the alteration refinement and constructibility descent. Step 9's lifting and finite descent are used for goodness only, with closed-base extension for the object identity. Step 14 meets the truncation-iso hypotheses (iso in degrees <= r, injective in degree r+1). In Step 15 pi=hi is finite, and finite detection holds because the unit is a stalkwise split injection. Step 18 uses full goodness for an arbitrary base morphism.
